title: Google gives the Pixel 11 Pro’s HiLight LED a much-needed feature
summary: HiLight now supports messages with the latest Android 17 QPR2 beta.
body: TL;DR Android 17 QPR2 Beta 6.1 introduces HiLight LED support for messages. If enabled, HiLight LED will glow twice when you receive a message from a favorite contact. A stable build of Android 17 QPR2 is expected in December. The Pixel 11 Pro’s HiLight was marketed as one of its highlight (pun intended) features. It glows when you get a call or when Gemini is working in the background, but unfortunately, it seems to weaken the Pixel’s flash . While Google can’t fix the flash issue, it is working to make HiLight more useful for Pixel users. With the Android 17 QPR2 Beta 6.1 update, the HiLight LED can glow when you receive a message from your favorite contacts (h/t 9to5Google ). This isn’t entirely surprising, as we spotted evidence pointing toward message integration alongside new HiLight colors yesterday. It’s worth noting that QPR2 Beta 6.1 doesn’t add any new colors for the HiLight LED; those might arrive in a later update.

title: OpenAI’s answer to Meta Muse is a cute AI agent that never clocks out
summary: The always-on AI agents can keep projects moving across your apps while you’re away.
body: TL;DR OpenAI’s new Dots are always-on AI agents that can keep working across connected apps even when you’re not actively chatting with them. A Dot can monitor ongoing work, suggest or complete next steps, and carry context across ChatGPT, Slack, and Teams. Dots are rolling out gradually to Pro, Business Premium, and Enterprise users in eligible markets. ChatGPT began as a place you opened when you needed an answer. Then ChatGPT Work pushed things further, taking on long-running jobs across apps and files. OpenAI’s next step is to make the AI stick around even after you close the chat. At DevDay 2026, the company unveiled Dots , always-on personal agents that can keep working toward your goals in the background. Powered by GPT-6 Astra , each Dot gets its own cloud computer and browser and can connect to more than 4,000 apps through OpenAI’s plugin ecosystem. OpenAI dresses them up as colorful, fuzzy characters you can name, but the idea goes deeper than a mascot. You can talk or message your Dot through ChatGPT, then reach the same agent through Slack or Microsoft Teams without losing context. Texting is coming soon.

While we just heard that GPT-6.1 Astra is getting sent back to the bench for misbehaving, progress continues on the rest of OpenAI’s headlining models, and this afternoon we’re getting the scoop on the first member of that 6.1-series to actually make its public debut, with the launch of GPT‑6.1 Sol. While we only just got GPT-6 Sol , OpenAI is not a company to rest on its laurels, and today is pushing right on forward with the evolution of GPT-6.1 Sol . Even though Astra remains the more capable model, with these 6.1 improvements, OpenAI reports that Sol is rapidly approaching Astra in “intelligence,” nearly matching the flagship model in performance across multiple metrics.

title: Android Auto bug is preventing calls from closed foldable phones
summary: You'll have to keep your phone open if you want to make a call.
body: Credit: Joe Maring / Android Authority TL;DR Motorola and Google are looking into an issue with Android Auto. Users report that they are unable to make outgoing calls while their flip phone is closed. The issue has been spotted on both Motorola’s and Samsung’s clamshell foldables. Part of the appeal of a clamshell foldable, like the Motorola Razr series , is being able to use it even when it’s in its smallest form. For example, you can run apps, check notifications, take selfies, and more. Normally, this also includes making calls while connected to Android Auto, but users have been experiencing issues recently. Both Motorola and Google are investigating an issue with Android Auto. The issue in question concerns clamshell foldable owners who can’t make calls on their phones. Specifically, when the phone is closed, outgoing calls don’t work. However, incoming calls are unaffected by the device’s state.

title: Your next Google Play subscription could work very differently
summary: New tools also add bundles, team seats, and smarter payment recovery.
body: TL;DR Google Play is adding usage-based subscription billing aimed at AI apps and other services with variable costs. New options will also support team subscriptions, mixed subscription/one-time purchases, and cross-app bundles. Google is also testing smarter grace periods, cancellation discounts, cheaper-plan offers, and Play Store winback deals. Google Play’s billing story changed earlier this year when Google opened the door wider to alternative billing systems and external web payments, giving Android users more choice over how they pay. Now it is turning its attention to subscriptions that still run through Google Play itself, with new billing options that could make AI apps, bundles, and failed payments work very differently for users. In a blog post , Google says it is testing and rolling out several new subscription options, including Usage-Based Billing. The new system targets services with variable costs, such as generative AI apps , and it lets users maintain a prepaid balance that can automatically top up when it drops below a set threshold. That opens the door to billing tied to consumption rather than only a fixed recurring amount.

Amazon’s car-centric Alexa accessory, the Echo Auto, has vanished from active sale on Amazon, leaving buyers to wonder whether the hardware giant is quietly pulling the plug on its in-car dongle. The missing listing was first flagged by users on Reddit , who were tracking upcoming seasonal sales and noticed the device was no longer discoverable via direct search queries.
